how_this_was_derived: Not supplied by the organisers -- reconstructed by querying the real file for its rarest security-relevant events. Among 9,125,382 records there are 1,272,524 failed admin logins but only 5 successes, 4 VPN tunnel events, 3 configuration changes and 2 admin-account object changes. Those 14 rare events are the planted attack; everything else is background noise. The derivation is reproducible: see scripts/discover_firex.py.
description: Multi-stage intrusion against a FortiGate firewall: reconnaissance by mass credential guessing, defence evasion by disabling logging and purging policy, successful administrative access from several external addresses, and finally a create-use-delete admin account cycle.

steps.label_note: Was T1562.002 (Disable Windows Event Logging), which does not apply to a firewall's disk log; corrected to the parent technique, Impair Defenses.
steps.evidence: Attribute 'status' of setting 'log disk setting' changed from 'enable' to 'disable'
Objects of 'firewall policy' were purged -- while logging was off
Administrator parul.sinha logged in successfully from https(8.42.69.77)
SSL VPN tunnel up; same account also used from 9.222.114.167 within 22 minutes
Administrator login successful, repeated at 03:47 and 04:17 from the same IP
Administrator svc_backup30 logged in successfully -- 6 minutes after the account was created
Delete system.admin svc_backup30 -- account destroyed 12 minutes after creation
